mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Business License) of the non-resident investor and of any intermediate holding company in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies / national company registry of the non-resident investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize each copy before a home-jurisdiction notary, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the home-jurisdiction competent authority, then submit a certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization path ONLY if the home jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention party: notarize, then authenticate at the home-country competent ministry, then obtain consular legalization at the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China, then submit a certified Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Active Status) of the non-resident investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Secretary of State / Registrar of Companies in the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the certificate, obtain Apostille from the home-country competent authority, then submit certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization path ONLY for non-Apostille states: notarize, authenticate domestically, legalize at the Chinese embassy/consulate, then submit certified Chinese translation. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the non-resident investor approving the establishment of the WFOE, appointing the registered legal representative, and authorizing the local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / corporate secretary / authorized notary of the non-resident investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: execute before a notary, notarize signatures, obtain Apostille from the home-jurisdiction competent authority, then submit certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization path ONLY for non-Apostille states: notarize, foreign-affairs legalization, then PRC consular legalization, then certified Chinese translation. Never combine the two routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association / constitutional instruments / bylaws of the non-resident investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry and/or corporate secretary of the non-resident investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certified copying, notarization, Apostille from the home-state competent authority, then certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization path ONLY for non-Apostille states: notarized certified copy, home-country government authentication, Chinese consulate legalization, then certified Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative channels only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter of the non-resident investor evidencing account relationship, standing, and absence of adverse credit information
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the non-resident investor's corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank officer signature notarized, notarization apostilled by the home-country competent authority, then certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization path ONLY for non-Apostille states: bank signature notarized, public authenticator legalized by home-country foreign-affairs authority, then legalized by the Chinese consulate, then certified Chinese translation. The channels are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Register of Directors and Shareholders of the non-resident investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent, corporate service provider, or company registry in the non-resident investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarized current certificate, Apostille from home-jurisdiction competent authority, then certified Chinese translation. Consular Legalization path ONLY for non-Apostille states: notarized current certificate, home-country authentication, PRC consular legalization, then certified Chinese translation. No chaining of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding, the WFOE's ultimate beneficial owner, legal representative, directors, senior managers, and signatories must be automatically screened and continuously refreshed against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; China's domestic terrorism, organized crime, and proscribed organizations lists issued by the Ministry of Public Security; OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List including the 50% ownership rule; UK HMT and EU consolidated financial sanctions; FATF high-risk jurisdiction and non-cooperative jurisdiction lists; and World Bank debarment lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all politically exposed persons, their family members, close associates, and remote beneficial owners, with independent verification of source of funds and source of wealth. Any exact, fuzzy, or indirect ownership connection requires a second-level review by the AML/CFT compliance officer, and any suspicious transaction or match must be reported to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center within 24 hours in accordance with the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Registration Integrated Online Service Platform (National One-Stop Enterprise Registration and E-Certification System) operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local municipal/provincial Administration for Market Regulation where the WFOE will be domiciled.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official statutory name of the WFOE must be in simplified Chinese characters. The legal name must follow the four-tier convention: administrative division + distinct trade name + industry or business characteristic + company form, e.g., City-Trade Mark-Technology-Limited Liability Company. The industry identifier must truthfully cover ISIC 6201 and may include 'Technology', 'Network', 'Software', 'Information', or 'Digital' as permitted by local administrative rules. Pinyin transliteration is accepted only as an auxiliary English trade name or registered trademark; it cannot replace the Chinese statutory name. The Chinese name cannot contain Arabic numerals alone, Latin letters, prohibited tokens, or misleading industry descriptions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within the initial 30-day name-reservation window, the applicant may apply online to extend the reservation once for another 30 days. If the name application is rejected, the applicant should first file a revised name online. If the rejection is formally confirmed, the applicant may, within 60 days of the rejection notice, file a written petition for administrative reconsideration with the immediately superior market-regulation authority, attaching the rejection decision, the original name-reservation filing, and evidence of compliance with the four-tier statutory name structure and prohibited-token rules. If administrative reconsideration is denied or no decision is issued within the statutory period, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit at the competent People's Court within six months of the reconsideration decision. The appeal must also demonstrate that the requested name does not infringe prior registered trademarks, well-known marks, or existing enterprise names.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for the low-code website-builder business in practice. The local Administration for Market Regulation requires a fixed, non-residential commercial address evidenced by the original real-estate ownership certificate or a lease registered with the tax authority. A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or shared service address without physical dedicated working space is rejected by the market regulator, by the State Taxation Administration during VAT registration and invoice-quota approval, and by commercial banks during corporate account opening because on-site verification will fail. The WFOE must maintain a physical place of business with office equipment and personnel proportionate to the software-development and no-code SaaS scope; a purely virtual setup will expose the entity to address-abnormality and bank-account restrictions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by municipal tax, market-regulation, or public-security authorities within the first 12 months is 20-35%, rising to 40% when VAT invoice quota, refunds, or cross-border technology-service preferences are applied for. Inspection checklist: (1) original lease and property-ownership documentation; (2) business license conspicuously displayed; (3) actual personnel present during normal business hours; (4) office signage matching the registered Chinese name; (5) functioning computers, servers, network equipment, and software-development environment consistent with ISIC 6201; (6) utility bills, access logs, and office-use evidence; (7) written confirmation from the landlord and neighboring tenants; (8) consistency between registered-address data and actual management location in the national enterprise information database. Non-compliance can result in being marked as a business-address abnormality, suspension of VAT invoice quota, removal from the address-normalization database, and freezing or restriction of the corporate bank account.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), particularly the chapters governing limited liability company formation, articles of association, registered capital, shareholder capital contribution obligations, corporate governance organs, legal representatives and statutory books; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020) and its Implementing Regulations; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (2021), especially provisions concerning establishment registration, registered items and filing of legal representatives.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), administered locally by the Market Supervision Administration (MSA) of the city or district where the registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise under current PRC law; the registered capital is determined by the sole shareholder in the Articles of Association. The 2023 Company Law requires a limited liability company shareholder to pay its subscribed capital in full within five years from incorporation, or within a shorter period stated in the Articles. No blocked escrow account or capital verification certificate is required for an ISIC 6201 software and no-code website builder company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD (adopted by the sole shareholder in accordance with the Articles of Association and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China). WHEREAS the sole shareholder has approved the formation of CN_WFOE_LTD as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company and has submitted the executed Articles of Association to the Market Supervision Administration; and WHEREAS this first resolution is intended to approve the post-registration corporate actions required for the Company to commence lawful software and digital services operations. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS. 1. Statutory Incorporation and Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company, with the share capital and classes of shares set forth in the Articles of Association, is ratified; the sole shareholder's subscription to all issued shares is accepted; and the legal representative shall record the subscription in the shareholder register, issue share certificates, and ensure that each capital contribution is paid in accordance with the contribution schedule contained in the Articles of Association and the mandatory five-year contribution period prescribed by applicable PRC law. 2. Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be the address set out in the lease agreement filed with the Market Supervision Administration, and such office shall serve as the Company's official seat, mailing address and place for maintaining the shareholder register and statutory books. 3. Banking and Payment System Authorization. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open RMB and foreign currency bank accounts at licensed commercial banks, and that the legal representative, the designated finance manager and the chief financial officer, if any, be and each is hereby authorized, individually or jointly as required by the bank's mandate, to sign account-opening documents, transfer instructions, checks and electronic payment authorizations. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED, that the legal representative and executive director, the supervisor and the manager named in the Articles of Association be and are hereby appointed as the statutory officers of the Company, with the legal representative vested with full power to represent the Company before the Market Supervision Administration, tax authority, social security office, banks and other government bodies. 5. Ratification of Pre-Incorporation Acts and Further Assurances. RESOLVED, that all lawful actions taken by the formation agent and the sole shareholder in connection with the formation of the Company are ratified; and the legal representative and the manager are authorized to make all governmental filings, tax registrations, social insurance registrations, seal engravings and other filings necessary to complete the Company's establishment and operational readiness. This resolution shall remain in full force and effect unless amended by a subsequent resolution of the shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Reservation and Authentication of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Online enterprise registration portal of the local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor shall first complete an online enterprise name reservation through the local MSA integrated government service platform, selecting the company type 'foreign-invested limited liability company' and entering the proposed Chinese and English names. Simultaneously, the investor shall settle the exact business scope, adopting the WFOE's Articles of Association in notarized or signature-verified form. If the name contains any element restricted by the foreign investment negative list, the MSA will reject it and require revision. The application shall clearly state the registered capital, sole shareholder profile, legal representative and registered office intention. This step is mandatory before formal establishment to secure name availability and to identify whether any special pre-approval is required. After online preliminary review, the investor may be required to present the original notarized foreign investor certificate at the service window.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese and English names, with three alternative names
Executed Chinese and English Articles of Association
Certificate of incorporation or equivalent business registration certificate of the sole foreign shareholder
Notarized and consular-legalized corporate documents of the foreign shareholder, as applicable
Passport copies of the proposed legal representative, executive director, supervisor and manager
Power of attorney appointing the formation agent, if used
Foreign investment negative list self-assessment memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSA denies or queries the name, the attorney shall submit three alternative names within two working days and correct any conflict with the negative list. If legalization of foreign investor documents is rejected, obtain a newer notarized copy from the home-country registry and re-submit through consular authentication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Market Supervision Administration (MSA) of the district or city where the registered office is located, under SAMR, through the online integrated government service portal or physical service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon obtaining the name approval, the formation attorney will submit the Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company to the same Market Supervision Administration via its online integrated service portal or in-person window. The application shall incorporate the approved registered name, registered office lease, property ownership certificate, original notarized documents from the foreign shareholder, appointment forms for the legal representative, executive director, supervisor and manager, and the executed Articles of Association. The Market Supervision Administration will verify the business scope, registered capital, legal representative identity and whether the proposed address is lawful. After approval, the Administration issues a Business License with a Unified Social Credit Code. The Company must promptly check the accuracy of the license, print the duplicate, and arrange engraving of the company, legal representative, finance, invoice and contract seals through an authorized public-security-controlled engraving vendor.
required_dossiers: Name pre-approval acceptance notice or reservation number
Duly executed Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder
Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company
Registered office lease agreement and landlord's property ownership certificate
Appointment letter and identification documents for legal representative, executive director, supervisor and manager
Certificate of incorporation and legalized identity documents of the foreign shareholder
Power of attorney and passport copy of the person submitting the filing
Consent documents for any special regulatory pre-approvals, if applicable; not applicable for ISIC 6201
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSA issues an incomplete-materials notice, respond within the statutory deadline, normally 15 working days, by uploading corrected documents. If the registered address is refused because the landlord's certificate is defective, procure a revised lease and a valid property certificate, or change the registered address to a qualified office and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Social Insurance and Housing Fund Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Tax Service of the State Taxation Administration (STA); local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; local Housing Fund Management Center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company must complete tax registration with the State Taxation Administration's local tax service through the electronic tax portal within thirty days after the business license is issued. The tax authority shall enroll the new taxpayer, set the tax category for software and digital services, and determine whether the Company should be classified as a small-scale taxpayer or general value-added taxpayer. The legal representative and financial officer must complete real-name verification and bind their identities to the Unified Social Credit Code. In parallel, the Company shall carry out social insurance registration for all employees with the local human resources and social security bureau and open a housing provident fund account. The Company must configure the electronic invoicing system and apply for an initial VAT invoice allocation. These registrations should be completed before invoicing any subscription customers through Stripe or Paddle.
required_dossiers: Business License (original and scanned copy)
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Legal representative and tax accounting personnel identification
Lease agreement and registered office proof
Articles of Association and foreign shareholder documents
Expected monthly revenue and expense information for taxpayer classification
Employee roster, social insurance enrollment forms and housing fund registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax enrollment is queried, the accountant should correct the registered business scope or financial system records and resubmit through the tax portal. If social insurance records lag, coordinate with the social security officer to reconcile employee listings and registration dates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Foreign Direct Investment Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in China and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through delegated bank filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The WFOE shall open its corporate RMB and foreign currency settlement accounts at a licensed commercial bank by presenting the business license, company seal, legal representative seal, finance seal, Unified Social Credit Code, the board resolution approving bank authorities, the registered office lease, and the personal identification documents of each authorized signatory. The bank will conduct anti-money laundering due diligence and a beneficial ownership check on the foreign shareholder. After the account number is generated, the bank shall file the Foreign Direct Investment registration with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange or complete the SAFE record by delegated electronic submission. The registered capital contribution from the overseas shareholder must be remitted into the designated capital account, and the bank will verify the receipt and transaction purpose against the registered capital schedule. The Company should obtain the SAFE filing sequence code and transaction receipts to evidence lawful inbound capital.
required_dossiers: Business License original
Company seal, legal representative seal, finance seal, invoice seal and contract seal
Banking authorization board resolution
Identification documents of each bank signatory and legal representative
Lease agreement and property certificate
Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation
FDI/SAFE registration forms provided by the bank
Articles of Association and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to compliance issues, engage another licensed bank or submit additional beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declarations. For SAFE registration defects, the bank will return the filing; the attorney shall supplement the foreign investor's certificate, power of attorney or board resolution and resubmit the FDI registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal, Tax Invoice Activation and Operational Readiness Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving unit; Local Tax Service (STA); Local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The final readiness phase involves procuring all company seals from an authorized engraving unit approved by the public security authority, and filing specimen seals with banks, tax office and social security agency. The Company should activate the taxpayer e-invoice system, set up payroll and social insurance rules in the human resources platform, and execute commercial leases or service agreements for office space. Because the registered scope is ISIC 6201, covering software and no-code website builder tools, no industrial operating license, environmental impact assessment or Civil Defense fire permit is required. The Company nonetheless must comply with general office fire safety and workplace safety obligations, and maintain proper records of the software subscription offering for tax and corporate books. Once these steps are completed, the Company may begin contracting with Stripe or Paddle payment processors and issue lawful invoices to customers.
required_dossiers: Business License and seal carving filing certificates
Tax enrollment and e-invoice system activation confirmation
Appointment records for statutory officers
Social insurance and housing fund registration confirmations
Office lease and fire-safety compliance certificate from building management
Bank account opening confirmation and SAFE filing receipt
Software subscription service contracts and pricing documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal filing is suspended, use an alternative authorized engraving bureau and request expedited approval. If the tax invoice quota is insufficient, submit an adjustment application with projected revenue evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital service under ISIC 6201. No physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly or warehousing operations are authorized by the registered business scope. If physical operations are added later, the local Market Supervision Administration and the Ministry of Emergency Management would become relevant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no mandatory industrial operating permit is required for visual web template, low-code web application and no-code website builder software services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no physical project subject to the Law of the People's Republic of China on Environmental Impact Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no full EIA Report, preliminary EIA or environmental registration is required for software-only business premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no regulated wastewater, VOC emissions or hazardous waste streams arise from ISIC 6201 digital services. General office waste disposal under municipal sanitation rules applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial Civil Defense fire permits. General commercial office premises must maintain fire extinguishers, evacuation signage, emergency lighting and comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China and local fire code. No Civil Defense certification is required for software-only office operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), operating the National Electronic Tax Bureau (E-Tax) electronic portal at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn, with provincial and municipal tax service branches administering VAT and enterprise income tax filings on the same portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company, the statutory Tax Identification Number is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on the business license. Procedure: (1) the foreign investors file for enterprise name pre-approval and WFOE incorporation through the State Administration for Market Regulation online system; (2) after SAMR approves the establishment and issues the business license bearing the USCC, tax registration is automatically completed under the 'Multiple Certificates in One' reform because the STA receives the incorporation data electronically; no separate TIN application is required; (3) the legal representative completes real-name authentication on E-Tax and files supplementary taxpayer information, including accounting standard, bank account details, VAT taxpayer type preference, and invoice issuance entitlement; (4) the E-Tax system then activates the WFOE as either a general VAT taxpayer or small-scale VAT taxpayer and authorises the issuance of full digital e-invoices. A foreign non-resident parent entity has no automatic PRC TIN; if it derives China-source income independently without a permanent establishment, it must register with the competent tax authority through a domestic withholding agent or obtain a non-resident enterprise tax registration limited to that China-source activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax system does not provide check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch entity elections. The only relevant election is VAT status: a taxpayer whose annual taxable sales are below the RMB 5,000,000 general taxpayer threshold may voluntarily elect general VAT taxpayer status if its accounting and tax records satisfy statutory requirements; otherwise small-scale taxpayer status is default.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VAT registration is mandatory for every enterprise upon SAMR business licensing; it is not triggered by turnover. For general VAT taxpayer classification, the mandatory threshold is annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000; a below-threshold taxpayer may remain a small-scale taxpayer unless it elects general status. Small-scale taxpayers currently benefit from the RMB 100,000 monthly VAT exemption policy but remain registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (full digital e-invoice) regime under the STA Golden Tax Phase IV system. Invoices must be issued through the National Electronic Tax Bureau or an STA-approved e-invoice service platform; the system assigns a unique electronic invoice number and a tax-control verification stamp in near real time, transmits the invoice record to the national VAT invoice electronic database, and enables transaction-level comparison with customs, forex, bank settlement, and enterprise income tax data. Taxpayers using enterprise resource planning systems may connect through API to the e-invoice issuance platform; paper VAT invoices remain only for legacy scenarios where full digital e-invoicing is not yet applied.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, 0% VAT applies when goods are legally exported from mainland China under a customs export declaration and the payments are received in foreign exchange or cross-border RMB from non-resident buyers. For the no-code website builder service (ISIC 6201 software and IT services), 0% VAT and associated exemption apply under Ministry of Finance and STA Circular 36 (2016) when: (i) the service is supplied to a non-resident enterprise or individual located outside mainland China; (ii) the service is wholly consumed outside the customs territory; (iii) the consideration is received in foreign exchange or cross-border RMB from abroad; and (iv) the taxpayer files the cross-border taxable service zero-rating/exemption declaration and retains the contract, service specification, issued zero-rated e-invoice, payment receipt, and evidence of overseas delivery and use. Pure online software-as-a-service delivery does not require customs clearance, but the documentary bundle must prove foreign consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Declaration Form) for physical export shipments
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing export of goods from mainland China
Bank Foreign Exchange Collection Voucher (statutory export proceeds receipt, equivalent to an inward remittance certificate)
Export sales contract and commercial invoice
Zero-rated full digital e-invoice or cross-border taxable service zero-rating declaration accepted by the STA
Foreign recipient tax identification and service delivery/consumption evidence for offshore digital services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA Golden Tax Phase IV system cross-matches VAT invoices, customs export declarations, foreign exchange collection data, and bank settlement records. A zero-rated export declaration will be rejected and output VAT assessed at the applicable domestic rate (6% for IT/no-code services; 13% for goods) where the documentation is incomplete, the foreign-exchange proceeds are not received within 180 days, or the service is found to be consumed in mainland China. Recovery adds daily late-payment surcharge at 0.05%, an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63, and a specific penalty of one to five times the refund obtained under Article 66. If the false export or zero-rating claim constitutes fraudulent export tax-refund crime under the PRC Criminal Law, responsible persons are subject to imprisonment of up to life imprisonment and monetary fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China and its wholly administered State Administration of Foreign Exchange
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a modern, structurally controlled foreign exchange regime. The Chinese Renminbi is fully convertible on current account transactions, covering bona fide trade in goods and services, dividends, royalties and ordinary operating expenses, subject to authenticity verification and tax compliance. Capital account transactions, however, remain tightly supervised by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. Inbound direct investment into a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise is permitted after completion of the FDI registration and establishment of a dedicated foreign exchange capital account. The WFOE may settle foreign currency capital into Renminbi only for genuine business expenditures within the permitted negative list framework; speculative investment in domestic equity or real estate is prohibited. Profit remittance to the overseas parent is treated as a current account item and is generally allowed, but the paying bank must receive a certified Chinese audit report, corporate income tax return, tax payment confirmation, board resolution declaring the dividend, and a valid SAFE registration. Surrender obligations for export proceeds have been abolished since 2012; enterprises may retain receipts in foreign currency accounts or settle voluntarily. Nevertheless, all receipts must be repatriated to China within prescribed timing, reported through the banking system, and supported by underlying transaction documents, invoices, and customs records. The practical effect for a low-code software exporter is that cash flow can move with relative efficiency, but every cross-border leap requires documentary discipline and alignment with SAFE circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory percentage conversion in current law. Export foreign currency receipts generated by the WFOE must be repatriated to a domestic foreign exchange account through approved channels within 120 days of shipment or service delivery, unless an extension is approved by the local SAFE branch. The enterprise may voluntarily choose between retaining the proceeds in foreign currency and converting to Renminbi, but all transactions must be reported using the correct trade and settlement purpose codes and matched with underlying contracts, invoices, and bank statements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account
Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account
Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech electronic money institutions, including digital EMI platforms promoted by Hong Kong or Singapore-licensed providers, possess only very limited legal viability for a mainland WFOE. Because the RMB is restricted to domestic financial institutions holding PBOC banking licenses, any payment or settlement solution must eventually clean through a Chinese bank. Offshore EMIs cannot issue a primary onshore bank account number for a WFOE, cannot participate in SAFE FDI registration, and cannot act as the sole treasury operator. Their practical utility is confined to ancillary collection channels for overseas customers, often working as merchant-of-record payment facilitators. Legally, they are barred from providing core bank account services in mainland China, and any attempt to bypass domestic clearing rails would violate the Administration of Foreign Exchange and Payment Institution regulations. Therefore the onboarding viability is rated Low. The WFOE must maintain its primary operational currency account with a licensed domestic commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative of the WFOE, normally a director or general manager, is required to appear physically at the chosen bank branch to open the basic deposit account, present the original business license, valid passport or Chinese ID, the company chop, the articles of association, the SAFE Foreign Investment Information Report, and the unified social credit code certificate. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for the initial corporate account setup. In exceptional cases where the legal representative cannot travel, a local manager may attend with a notarized power of attorney that has been apostilled or consular-legalized in the home jurisdiction, plus a board resolution explicitly designating the account signatory. The bank compliance team may still require a video interview with the legal representative and the beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ubiquitous holding-structure opacity triggering ultimate beneficial owner uncertainty for the Chinese bank's AML risk classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full ownership chart from the parent entity through every intermediary holding company to the final natural persons, supported by corporate registry certificates, constitutional documents, registers of members, and notarized UBO declarations. Include passports, proof of address, and a board resolution confirming the absence of undisclosed beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident founder, high-net-worth individual, or politically exposed person status causing enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth scrutiny and transaction-profile alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a professional background screening report from a recognized counterparty compliance database, sworn source-of-wealth declaration covering the origin of the equity injection, two years of bank statements from the remitting institution, tax residence certificates, and a legal opinion from an approved Chinese law firm assessing PEP-related risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared software subscription business model and the banking expectation of physical-goods trade documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the finalized WFOE software product documentation, standardized end-user license agreement, GDPR and Chinese data security compliance certifications, detailed pricing schedules, sample customer invoices, merchant-of-record statements from Stripe and Paddle, and an independent IT audit confirming the digital nature of the transaction flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Profit remittance or dividend declaration trigger involving tax-law inconsistencies between reported revenue and distributable earnings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the Chinese certified audit report, complete corporate income tax annual filing, tax payment receipts, the official tax clearance certificate for the relevant fiscal year, a shareholders' resolution declaring the dividend, and the SAFE notification confirming the WFOE's imported direct investment equities can support the remittance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The overseas shareholder must effect the transfer exclusively through SWIFT MT103 from a recognized correspondent bank into the WFOE's designated Foreign Exchange Capital Account opened with the Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank. The remittance instruction must clearly reflect a capital injection purpose code compatible with SAFE's direct investment classification, and the remitter's KYC file must support the identity and ownership of the company. Immediately after receipt, the WFOE must complete the SAFE FDI registration if not already finalized, file the Foreign Investment Information Report with the local market supervision authority, obtain a capital verification audit report from a Chinese certified public accountant, and deposit settlement proceeds in a RMB settlement account linked to the capital account. Every withdrawal from the capital settlement account must be matched with genuine business purpose evidence, including contracts, invoices, payroll records, and rent confirmations, and within the scope permitted by China's foreign investment negative list.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For international subscription platform disbursements and cloud infrastructure payments, the primary clearing rail will be SWIFT MT103 bank telegraphic transfers routed through the WFOE's domestic bank, supported by the underlying digital service agreement, payment processor payout statements, and proper transaction purpose codes for software licensing and internet services. For larger fixed-asset purchases or infrastructure outsourcing contracts involving tangible goods, the treasury may additionally utilize commercial letters of credit, which allow the Chinese bank to guarantee payment against shipping and customs documents. Documentary collections provide a lower-cost alternative for repeat non-risk counterparties, where the exporter forwards draft and documents through two banks without an on-demand guarantee. For domestic Chinese supplier transactions, the WFOE should use the People's Bank of China clearing system via RMB current account to avoid unnecessary FX conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts with real demand backing under SAFE's true-need and risk-hedging principles
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for foreign currency syndicated loans and long-term capital account liabilities
FX swap contracts between Renminbi and US dollars for renewable periods, limited to actual operating exposure
Onshore exchange-traded and OTC currency options for non-speculative hedging of current account receipts and payments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Filing (Annual CIT Return and Supporting Financial Statement Package)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the local in-charge tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 31 of the following year for a calendar-year WFOE; within five months after the approved fiscal year-end for non-calendar taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily late-payment interest of 0.05% of overdue tax accrues from the day after the statutory deadline until full settlement; failure-to-file fines range from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; underpayment or evasion may trigger a penalty of 50% to 500% of the short-paid tax, asset freezes, compulsory enforcement, tax blacklisting, and loss of administrative good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Credit Information Report (Annual Report to SAMR / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the local market regulation bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 - June 30 in each year for the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is placed on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operating Records within 10 working days after the June 30 deadline; if the abnormal listing remains unrectified for three consecutive years, the company is moved to the List of Seriously Illegal and Dishonest Enterprises, triggering cross-agency credit sanctions, restricted government procurement and financing, enhanced inspections, and possible forced deregistration or license revocation by SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (Foreign Investment Annual Information Return under the Foreign Investment Law)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR via the integrated National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 - June 30 in each year for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false or misleading filing triggers a MOFCOM/SAMR correction order; continued refusal to correct may attract administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures with a statutory ceiling of RMB 500,000, adverse credit-record marking, inclusion in the abnormal operating list, and eventual forced deregistration if non-compliance persists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Information Confirmation and Event-Driven UBO / Share Transfer Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR through the local enterprise registration authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation is due within the January 1 - June 30 annual reporting window; any shareholding transfer, change of actual controller, ultimate controller, or beneficial owner must be reported within 30 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report, late reporting, or false beneficial-owner information triggers a SAMR correction order and, upon continued non-compliance, administrative penalties of up to RMB 50,000 per occurrence under the Beneficial Owner Information Administration Measures; the company may also be listed as abnormal or seriously dishonest, and may face license revocation or deregistration if violations persist.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Related-Party Transaction Statement and Transfer Pricing Compliance Package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual enterprise income tax settlement by May 31; contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, if triggered, must be completed by June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or defective filing of the related-party statement may attract failure-to-file fines of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation exposes the taxpayer to reassessment, daily default interest of 0.05% on any tax underpayment, and penalties of 50% to 500% of the short-paid tax in evasion cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements Audit and CPA Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent certified Chinese CPA firm; audited financial statements kept at the registered office and produced to shareholders, SAMR, or STA on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements and the CPA audit report must be completed within four months after the fiscal year-end (April 30 for a calendar-year WFOE) and in any event before the May 31 CIT filing if the audited statements are relied upon for tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and audit annual financial statements violates the PRC Company Law and Accounting Law, exposing the legal representative and accounting responsible person to administrative fines, correction orders, and regulatory credit-listing; absence of a CPA audit report may also lead to disallowed tax deductions, tax authority assessment, and reputational damage.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All limited liability companies, including a WFOE, are subject to a statutory annual audit by an independent certified Chinese CPA firm under PRC Company Law; there is no ordinary turnover, balance-sheet, or headcount exemption for a foreign-invested private company. Quantitative triggers for related-party and transfer pricing filing obligations arise under STA Bulletin 42 (2016) where aggregate related-party tangible-goods transactions exceed RMB 200 million, aggregate related-party financial transactions exceed RMB 100 million, or aggregate related-party intangible/services transactions exceed RMB 40 million in a tax year, each requiring enhanced contemporaneous documentation and, in specified cases, certified valuation or audit support. Listed issuers, licensed financial institutions, insurance companies, securities and futures firms, trust companies, and state-controlled enterprises are separately mandated to undergo independent audits without regard to size. Thus the ordinary WFOE audit obligation is triggered at zero turnover unless a formal dormant-company exemption is expressly granted by the applicable accounting or company law rules, which is rare and must be documented.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), being the local GAAP converged with IFRS; small qualifying enterprises may apply the Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises; IFRS-based reporting applies to listed issuers in relevant regulatory contexts; financial statements must be prepared in RMB using the accrual basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China requires beneficial owner and foreign investment information reporting through SAMR and MOFCOM. A WFOE must report its beneficial owner information at registration and annually confirm such information during the January 1 - June 30 annual reporting window. Any equity or share transfer, change of actual controller, change of ultimate controller, or change of beneficial owner must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the change. If the transfer alters foreign investor identity or foreign ownership percentages, the Foreign Investment Information annual report must also be updated within the same 30-day event-driven reporting window. The annual confirmation does not replace the event-driven 30-day filing duty, and the shareholder register must be updated contemporaneously with each transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 per annum for a typical small-to-mid-market WFOE

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate is 25% under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 4. Available incentives for a qualifying no-code website builder WFOE include: (i) Small Low-Profit Enterprise relief reducing effective rate to 5% if annual taxable income does not exceed RMB 3,000,000, with taxable income reduced to 25% of the actual amount and a 20% rate applied; (ii) 100% super deduction for qualified Research and Development expenses under CIT Law Article 30 and its implementing rules; (iii) reduced 15% rate in certain free trade zones or regional preferential zones if statutory substantive operations and industry conditions are met; and (iv) 10% rate for a certified National Key Software Enterprise satisfying criteria on core IP, R&D intensity, revenue from software, and technical personnel. Losses may generally be carried forward for 5 years, and 10 years for qualified high-tech or small low-profit enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return Form A (A100000 and supporting schedules) filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic filing portal, commonly referred to as the e-Tax filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement combined with quarterly or monthly provisional prepayments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Provisional Corporate Income Tax returns must be filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter or month. The annual settlement return is due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., by 31 May of the following calendar year for a 31 December year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate operating revenue recognized under PRC Accounting Standards, including software subscription fees, no-code website builder plan fees, license fees, and related service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert foreign-currency revenue to RMB at the prevailing spot rate or monthly/quarterly average rate used in accounting. Revenue from cross-border platform sales or cloud-based no-code services must be reconciled against the withholding tax declarations for any related outbound royalty or technical service portions. If the contract bundles software license and hosting services, separate the royalty component from the service component to align CIT recognition, VAT treatment, and non-resident WHT obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to revenue, including cloud hosting charges, data center fees, domain acquisition costs, employee wages, software amortization, and infrastructure overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident cloud, infrastructure, and SaaS providers must be classified as services versus royalties. Pure hosting and connectivity fees are generally not subject to withholding tax if no Chinese permanent establishment exists, while payments for the use of or right to use software intellectual property may be characterized as royalties subject to 10% statutory WHT or a reduced treaty rate. Review the related-party transaction schedules and ensure any non-resident payment is supported by a Contract Withholding Tax receipt or a treaty relief filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible taxes and surcharges other than Corporate Income Tax and VAT itself, including urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duty, property tax, and land use tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT is not included in the CIT expense stream and must not be deducted. Where the WFOE contractually bears the non-resident seller's Chinese WHT under a gross-up arrangement, such borne tax is generally not deductible as a statutory tax expense unless the tax is imposed on the WFOE itself; otherwise add it back in the tax adjustment section. Properly classify royalty-related stamp duty and cross-border service contract taxes to avoid duplicated deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Lines 4-6 - Selling, Administrative and Financial Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing expenses, management salaries and overhead, financial expenses including interest on intercompany debt, bank charges, and foreign exchange losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees and head-office cost allocations must demonstrate actual services rendered, benefit to the WFOE, and arm's length pricing; purely profit-stripping service fees are non-deductible. Interest paid to a non-resident related lender is capped by the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalization ratio for non-financial enterprises; disallowed excess interest must be added back in Box 7. Retain contemporaneous evidence of the loan purpose, commercial rationale, group credit rating, and arm's length interest rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating items such as gains or losses on disposal of equipment or intangible assets, government grants, donations, fines, and penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible fines and administrative penalties must be added back. If the WFOE receives a subsidy for software industry development, determine whether it is taxable government grants or qualified non-taxable income; if non-taxable, complete the separate non-taxable income schedule. Cross-border IP disposals involving a non-resident seller may expose the seller to China-source capital gains tax and require a withholding declaration; ensure the relevant treaty capital gains article and China domestic source rules are analyzed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax computed under PRC Accounting Standards, representing the starting point for tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the accounting profit to the audited financial statements. Any proposed transfer pricing adjustment from the tax authority is not booked in financial statements but is reflected in the taxable income reconciliation via the special tax adjustment schedules. Intentionally misstating Box 6 to conceal taxable profit creates legal exposure under the Tax Collection Law and may trigger tax fraud criminal examination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Lines 11-13 - Tax Adjustments, Exemptions and Additional Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of taxable income add-backs and reductions, including non-deductible expenses, related-party transfer pricing adjustments, tax-exempt income, and R&D super deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible royalties paid for a shell IP license, sham intercompany services, disallowed thin cap interest, and penalties. Use the R&D super deduction schedule to claim the 100% additional deduction for qualified software development and cloud platform R&D expenditures. Non-resident payments without valid withholding tax vouchers should still be analyzed on substance: if they fail the arm's length benefit test they must be added back even if reported to the tax bureau, and the absence of a withholding voucher will not cure the upstream WHT noncompliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of current taxable income by unexpired prior-year tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax losses generally expire after 5 years unless the 10-year extension applies to a qualified high-tech or small low-profit enterprise. Losses cannot be carried back. If there has been a change in equity ownership or a change in the principal business, verify that the continuity-of-business and ownership continuity tests under the CIT loss carryforward rules are satisfied; an impermissible change from a substantive no-code development operation to a passive licensing shell can trigger loss carryforward denial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 (Lines 17-19 - Taxable Income and Tax Rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after adjustments, multiplied by the applicable Corporate Income Tax rate (25%, 15%, 10%, or the effective 5% small low-profit rate).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty benefits are to be claimed on an outbound dividend, the dividend must be paid out of after-tax profits as reflected on this taxable income computation. Artificial reduction of taxable income through non-arm's-length related-party pricing will also reduce the dividend withholding tax base and, if structured to claim a lower treaty rate through a conduit, may be attacked under the Principal Purpose Test or beneficial ownership rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 (Lines 20-24 - Foreign Tax Credits, Prepayments and Balance Due)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax credits, reduction and exemption credits, quarterly prepayments already made, and final tax payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign corporate income tax paid on foreign-source income can be credited against Chinese CIT within the quota limits. Dividend withholding tax on distributions to the non-resident shareholder is not credited or reported on this return; it is enforced separately under the Contract Withholding Tax declaration. The balance of CIT due must be settled by 31 May; late payment triggers a daily surcharge of 0.05% on the overdue amount and potential penalties up to 50% of the underpaid tax if a false filing is found.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual CIT return within the statutory deadline may result in an administrative fine of RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious cases, plus daily late-payment surcharges of 0.05% on unpaid tax. Under-declaration through false reporting may be characterized as tax evasion under the Tax Collection Law Article 63, with a penalty of 50% to 5 times the evaded tax. Where the underpayment exceeds the thresholds under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, or where fraudulent invoicing or forged accounting records are present, criminal tax fraud liability may arise and responsible persons may be prosecuted for tax evasion punishable by imprisonment and fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a PRC resident enterprise such as the WFOE to a non-resident enterprise, imposed under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law and SAT withdrawal rules, unless the applicable Double Tax Treaty reduces the rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA dividend rate, the withholding agent or the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain from the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction a valid Certificate of Tax Residency covering the dividend payment date; (2) complete and file the non-resident treaty benefit claim/preservation form through the electronic tax portal or with the competent tax authority before or at the time of the payment; (3) submit a beneficial ownership statement with supporting evidence showing that the foreign shareholder has substance, genuine business purpose, and is not a conduit created mainly to obtain treaty benefits; (4) satisfy the holding period requirement, typically continuous direct shareholding of at least 25% for the lower treaty rate and in many treaties a 365-day ownership test for dividends; (5) ensure the income is not attributable to a permanent establishment in China; (6) upon denial or failure to perfect the claim, withhold at the statutory 10% rate and pay it over, with late interest and penalties if underwithheld. The procedure is a self-assessment/reporting regime rather than a general advance approval, but false treaty claims may be recharacterized under domestic anti-abuse law and the Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on China-source interest and royalties paid to non-resident enterprises is 10%, plus VAT and surcharges where the payment is characterized as a taxable service or deemed royalty. Under many Chinese DTAs, interest is reduced to 10%, 7%, or 5% and royalties to 10%, 7%, or 5% depending on the treaty and the beneficial owner status. For no-code and SaaS arrangements, a payment for a software license or the right to use a copyright in computer software is generally treated as a royalty; a pure cloud-hosting/data-processing service without transfer of intellectual property rights is generally treated as a business service and is taxable in China only if attributable to a permanent establishment. Intercompany debt interest in excess of the arm's length amount or the thin capitalization ratio is not deductible and may still carry WHT exposure on the de facto interest payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File documentation is statutorily required under CIT Law Article 42 and the SAT related-party transaction filing rules if the annual related-party transaction amount reaches any of the following thresholds: RMB 200,000,000 for tangible property transfers; RMB 100,000,000 for intangible property transfers; RMB 100,000,000 for related-party services; RMB 100,000,000 for financial asset transfers; or RMB 100,000,000 for related-party debt/investment arrangements. A Master File is additionally required when the aggregate annual related-party transaction amount reaches RMB 1,000,000,000 or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply the offshore Economic Substance Regulations as a separate statute, but the general anti-abuse rule under CIT Law Article 47, the arm's length principle under Article 41, and the beneficial ownership and Principal Purpose Test contained in applicable tax treaties operate together to require genuine economic substance. The WFOE must demonstrate that profits earned from no-code website builder software and related services correspond to functions performed, assets used, and risks assumed in China. Core Income-Generating Activities such as product development, customer contracting, pricing, billing, support, and risk management should occur in China through actual employees, premises, and decision-making. If these activities are performed outside China but the WFOE invoices for them, there may be a permanent establishment risk abroad; if the WFOE is a shell that merely invoices while the foreign parent performs all substantive functions, China can disregard its separate existence, reattribute profits, and deny treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is operated as a conduit with no employees, no physical presence, and no substantive decision-making in China, and dividends or royalties are routed through a low-tax intermediary beneficial owner to claim a reduced DTA withholding rate despite the absence of genuine commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The competent tax authority may invoke CIT Law Article 47 and Tax Collection Law Article 35 to recharacterize the arrangement, disregard the conduit entity, deny treaty benefits, and impose the full 10% statutory withholding tax or, if there is no treaty entitlement, 10% WHT plus daily late-payment interest at 0.05%. If the scheme constitutes intentional tax evasion, a penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax may be imposed under Tax Collection Law Article 63, and the entity may be included in the Major Tax Violation Case blacklist for public disclosure and administrative discipline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under PRC Company Law if the directors or shareholders abuse the separate legal personality of the WFOE to evade tax and harm creditors. Directors can be held personally and jointly liable for restitution of diverted assets, subjected to tax enforcement travel bans and exit restrictions if the company has unpaid tax, and blacklisted as de facto controllers. Where the arrangement is criminal tax evasion or fraud, the directors and the legal representative may face investigation under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years, fines, and disqualification from corporate management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Dividend/Withholding Declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE understates taxable profit by recording fictitious intercompany service fees, paying dividends under disguised loans or expense reimbursements without withholding tax, or filing false annual CIT returns to eliminate tax for the purpose of repatriating profit to foreign shareholders without taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Tax Collection Law Article 63, the tax authority will collect the unpaid tax and late-payment surcharge and impose a monetary penalty of 50% to 5 times the evaded tax. Article 64 applies where a false tax return is filed and the taxpayer fails to pay tax; serious fraud triggers criminal referral. PRC Criminal Law Article 201 provides imprisonment of up to 3 years or criminal detention, plus fines, where the evaded tax amount is relatively large and exceeds 10% of the tax payable; imprisonment of 3 to 7 years and fines apply where the amount is gigantic and exceeds 30%. A unit crime also makes the directly responsible supervisor and CFO liable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false tax returns, instruct concealment of revenue, or authorize undisclosed profit distributions are exposed to personal civil liability through corporate veil piercing. The tax authority may freeze the company's bank accounts, seize assets, and impose credit blacklisting on the legal representative. In criminal cases, the responsible directors and the person in charge may be sentenced to imprisonment of up to 7 years, receive criminal fines, and be ordered to make restitution. Travel bans and high-consumption restrictions operate under tax enforcement blacklisting mechanisms while the tax deficiency remains unpaid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Sham Intercompany Financing/IP Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE fails to prepare or produce the contemporaneous Local File and Master File when statutory thresholds are met, or enters into non-arm's-length royalty payments for shell intellectual property owned in another jurisdiction, excessive intercompany debt exceeding the 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio, or profit-stripping arrangements with functions, assets, and risks misaligned from economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under CIT Law Article 41 and the SAT transfer pricing documentation rules, the tax authority may apply the best method, make a transfer pricing adjustment, and impose special tax adjustment interest at the PBOC benchmark lending rate plus 5 percentage points for related-party adjustments. Under Tax Collection Law, an underpaid tax arising from false documentation or concealment can attract a penalty of 50% to 5 times the tax due, and the failure to provide required related-party documentation may support a re-estimation of taxable income and the denial of deductions. In egregious cases, the conduct is criminalized as tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute sham intellectual property licenses or artificial debt push-downs without commercial purpose may be liable when the company cannot pay its CIT deficiency because profits have been stripped out to related non-residents. PRC courts may lift the corporate veil and hold directors and controlling shareholders jointly liable to the extent of their abuse. Unpaid corporate tax can trigger asset preservation, travel bans, and blacklisting of the legal representative or de facto controller. If the sham arrangement is proven to be intentional concealment of taxable income, the directors face criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to 7 years, fines, and restitution of the evaded tax.
